newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Laidlaw to acquire EmCare for $400 million.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Laidlaw to acquire EmCare for $400 million.

text.p: (All figures U.S. dollars unless otherwise stated)

Canada's Laidlaw Inc. said on Wednesday that it agreed to buy EmCare Holdings Inc. for $400 million in cash and debt, expanding its emergency medical transportation operations into emergency room management.

Laidlaw said the cost includes $38 a share for EmCare's outstanding stock, $25 million associated with stock options and the assumption of $65 million in debt. Laidlaw is already North America's biggest emergency health care transportation, school busing and municipal transit firm.

EmCare, based in Dallas, provides services to hospital emergency departments, mainly physician recruitment and staffing as well as inpatient, primary and managed care services contracting. It is part of a $7 billion industry of outsourced physician services.

More than 90 percent of its $260 million yearly revenues is generated by the management of emergency departments under 131 contracts in 162 hospitals. EmCare operates in 21 states and contracts with 1,800 doctors who care for more than 3 million patients a year, the companies said.

"For some time, our intention has been to expand our role in the health care service industry into markets associated with the emergency transportation (services)," Laidlaw President James Bullock said.
"EmCare now provides Laidlaw with a platform for solid growth in the emergency physician practice management field," Bullock told analysts in a conference call.
He added that the deal, which requires that shareholders tender 51 percent of EmCare's shares, would not reduce Laidlaw's earnings. The deal is expected to close in early September.
EmCare Chairman Leonard Riggs and President William Miller will remain in their posts and EmCare will operate as a division of Laidlaw, Bullock said.
Riggs and Miller said they agreed to tender their EmCare shares, representing about 15 percent of the company's total stock outstanding.
Riggs told the conference call that EmCare, which last week closed a deal to serve up to nine facilities in Chicago, planned more acquisitions.
Miller added: "We have a number of targets sitting out there that we will be moving on and closing in the second half of the year.
Laidlaw's stock rose C20 cents to C$21.50 in late afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. EmCare fell 69 cents to $37.56 on Nasdaq.
